jamie_customer: hey team — customer hitting intermittent 502s and a bunch of "RuntimeError: Event loop is closed" traces from a long-lived Celery worker. They say it happens after ~8–12h of uptime and we've also seen duplicate charges because the client retried. repro steps + snippet below. any ideas?

```python
# worker.py (simplified)
import asyncio
from celery import Celery
from redwood import RedwoodClient

app = Celery()
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=...)

@app.task
def handle(item):
    # this calls into async code via existing event loop
    loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
    return loop.run_until_complete(client.generate(prompt=item['text']))
```

jamie_customer: stack trace (truncated):
```
RuntimeError: Event loop is closed
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/asyncio/base_events.py", line 612, in get_event_loop
    raise RuntimeError('no running event loop')
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/asyncio/runners.py", line 45, in run
    loop.run_until_complete(main())
```

emma_support: thanks — can you paste the redwood-py and httpx versions + whether you're running uvloop / container restarts? :eyes:

jamie_customer: redwood-py==0.10.2, httpx==0.23.3, uvloop enabled, container restarts are only when we do deploys (no scheduled restarts). this is a customer prod system (high QPS). saw duplicate payloads in our logs for requests that returned 502, then 200 (same prompt id).

kevin_sre: uvloop + long-running Celery + calling run_until_complete is a red flag. run_until_complete will re-use the loop object and if something calls loop.close() elsewhere you end up with "Event loop is closed" when a new task is scheduled. Are you using any libraries that call asyncio.run() or close loops at shutdown?

maria_eng: fyi there was a regression in 0.10.2 around background cleanup when the sync-wrapper interacts with httpx connection pooling + TaskGroup usage. it could lead to clients being closed unexpectedly (esp. with uvloop + forking workers). major clues: (1) errors manifest after hours, (2) retries lacking idempotency keys cause duplicate billing, (3) httpx pools get exhausted then falling back to retries.

emma_support: for the billing duplicates — please check if you're setting an Idempotency-Key on requests. if not, our platform will treat retries as distinct requests. quick workaround: attach an idempotency header derived from your job id. e.g. `headers={"Idempotency-Key": job_id}`.

jamie_customer: ok — we weren't setting idempotency keys. we can add that but curious if there's a short-term fix so we don't need a full library upgrade right away.

maria_eng: short-term mitigation options:
- explicitly close the client on worker shutdown: `await client.aclose()` (or `client.close()` in sync wrapper)
- avoid mixing `asyncio.run`/`run_until_complete` with manual loop management; prefer using a single loop per process
- disable uvloop as a quick test (it changes event loop policy)
- set httpx limits: `limits=TimeoutLimits(max_keepalive_connections=10)` to reduce pool exhaustion

kevin_sre: can you grep for `loop.close()` in your stack traces and post the full traceback if it reoccurs? also check whether your Celery worker is forking (prefork) — if so, create the client after the fork (not at module import time).

jamie_customer: good call — we create `RedwoodClient()` at import time in the module. we'll move it into the task body for now and add the Idempotency-Key. will report back after a few hours. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deployed redwood-py v0.11.1 to hosted infra (fix: sync-wrapper + httpx pool cleanup) — recommend customers on 0.10.x to upgrade.

maria_eng: also sending a small repro you can run locally (uses asyncio.TaskGroup to simulate long-run churn):
```python
import asyncio
from redwood import RedwoodClient

async def bang(i):
    client = RedwoodClient(api_key=...)
    try:
        await client.generate(prompt=f"hello {i}")
    finally:
        await client.aclose()

async def main():
    async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
        for i in range(1000):
            tg.create_task(bang(i))

asyncio.run(main())
```

emma_support: thanks everyone. action items: jamie_customer will (1) move client creation into task, (2) add Idempotency-Key header, (3) disable uvloop temporarily if problem persists, (4) upgrade to 0.11.1 when convenient. we'll keep monitoring billing and retries and reopen if we still see 502s.

jamie_customer: applying the changes now. will ping once stable. really appreciate the quick triage. :pray:
